data.text:
### General General state-scoped effects: | Name | Parameters | Examples | Description | Notes | Version Added | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | state_event | `id = `
The event to fire. `days = / `
Fires the event in the specified number of days. Optional.
`hours = / `
Fires the event in the specified number of hours. Optional.
`random = / `
Adds a random number (between *0* and *random*, inclusive) of **hours** to the scheduled fire time. Optional.
`random_days = / `
Adds a random number (between *0* and *random_days*, inclusive) of days to the scheduled fire time. Optional. | *(example below)* | Fires the specified event for the current state. | Where triggers do not need to be repeatedly checked `random` can be a performance light alternative to `mean_time_to_happen` for scheduling events. Using days = / or hours may still be bugged and will not fire the event. | 1.0 | | set_state_flag | ``
An unique string to identify the state flag with.
**OR**
`flag = `
The flag to set.
`days = `
Sets the flag to last for the specified amount of days. Optional.
`value = `
The new value of the flag on the scale from -2 147 483 648 to 2 147 483 647. | `set_state_flag = my_flag`*(example below)* | Defines a state flag. | No tooltip is shown. [The flag in this effect is used in the meaning of 'boolean flag', used to store information.]() | 1.0 | | clr_state_flag | ``
The unique string of a state flag to clear. | `clr_state_flag = my_flag` | Clears a defined state flag. | No tooltip is shown. | 1.0 | | modify_state_flag | `flag = `
The flag to modify.
`value = `
The value to add to the flag. Defaults to 0.
`days = `
The amount of days that the flag should last for before being cleared. Optional, defaults to permanent.
| *(example below)* | Adds an integer value to a flag. | The flag must be already set. | 1.3 | | set_state_name | ``
Defines the new name. | `set_state_name = "Funland"` | Changes the current state's name to the specified name. | | 1.3 | | reset_state_name | ``
Boolean. | `reset_state_name = yes` | Resets any changes to the current state's name. | | 1.3 | | add_claim_by | ` / `
The country to add the claim for. | `add_claim_by = SOV` | Adds a claim for the specified country on the current scope. | | 1.0 | | remove_claim_by | ` / `
The country to remove the claim for. | `remove_claim_by = SOV` | Removes a claim by the specified country on the current scope. | | 1.0 | | add_core_of | ` / `
The country to add the core for. | `add_core_of = SOV` | Adds a core for the specified country on the current scope. | | 1.0 | | remove_core_of | ` / `
The country to remove the core for. | `remove_core_of = SOV` | Removes a core for the specified country on the current scope. | | 1.0 | | set_demilitarized_zone | ``
Boolean. | `set_demilitarized_zone = yes` | Makes the current scope a demilitarized zone. | | 1.0 | | set_state_category | ``
The category to change to. | `set_state_category = rural` | Changes the current state category to the specified category. | Categories are found in `/Hearts of Iron IV/common/state_category/*.txt` | 1.3 | | add_state_modifier | **Modifier scope** ` = `
Adds a modifier to the state. | *(example below)* | Adds a [modifier]() to the current state. | | 1.3 | | add_manpower | ` / `
The amount to add. | `add_manpower = 10000` | Adds the specified amount of total population to the current state. | Note that when using negative manpower it will, besides reducing the population, also add directly to the recruitable manpower of the state. Which will increase your manpower | 1.0 | | add_resource | `type = `
The resource to add. `amount = / `
The amount to add. | *(example below)* | Adds the specified resource in the specified amount to the current state. | Can also be used in country scope. | 1.0 | | set_border_war | ``
Boolean. | `set_border_war = yes` | Enables Border War status for the current state. | Used for the state-based border wars, represented with orange stripes, see [§ Border wars](#Border_wars) for the border wars that simulate combat on a border between two countries. On the end of the border war, [the on_border_war_lost on action]() is fired for the state that where the border war was lost. | 1.0 | | create_unit | `division = `
The division string.
`owner = `
The owner of the division.
`prioritize_location = `
If possible, this province within the state gets used. Optional.
`allow_spawning_on_enemy_provs = yes`
Allows the units to be created on provinces owned by the division owner's enemy. Defaults to false.
`count = `
The amount of units to create. Defaults to 1.
`id = `
The ID to identify the unit. Only used in delete_unit.
`country_score = { ... }`
A MTTH block deciding the province in the state where the division should spawn, evaluates in the scope of the controller. Defaults to prioritising owner's controlled provinces first and then owner's allies.
`divisional_commander_xp = `
give the division commander experience on unit creation

The following arguments go within `division = ""`:
`name = \"\"`
The name of the division.
`division_template = \"\"`
The template to be used by the division.
`start_experience_factor = `
Experience of the division, with 0 being none and 1 being full training. Defaults to 1.
`start_equipment_factor = `
Equipment stockpile of the division. Defaults to 1.
`start_manpower_factor = `
Manpower stockpile of the division. Defaults to 1.
`force_equipment_variants = { = { owner = \"\" amount = version_name = \"\" } }`
Forces a certain type of equipment to be used. Multiple equipment types can be added by adding multiple = {} lines. | *(example below)* *(example below)* *(example below)* | Adds the specified division to the current state. | The division string **must be on one line**. A linebreak in the middle of `division = "..."` will break the effect and result in no units being spawned. **Can only be used within a state scope**, such as [capital_scope](). The effect will do nothing when put into a country's scope. **Equipment factor cannot be set to zero.** If set to zero, it will be treated as a 1. Created equipment will be the latest available to the country. | 1.3 | | teleport_armies | `limit = { }`
The condition that must be true for the owner of the armies for them to teleport. `to_state_array = `
The state array the armies will get teleported to.
`to_province = `
The province the armies will get teleported to.
`to_state = `
The state the armies will get teleported to.
| *(example below)* | Teleports all armies in the specified state if the owner of the armies meets the condition. | Only define one of to_state_array, to_state, or to_province. If none is specified, it defaults to the capital. | 1.9 | | add_province_modifier | `static_modifiers = { }`
The list of modifiers.
`province = `The province to apply the modifiers to.`provinces = {}`Scope for selecting multiple provinces. The following arguments have to go inside it:
`id = `The ID of the province. Multiple can be specified.
`all_provinces = yes`Selects all provinces to which the limitations apply. T
